p01.why: An anonymous union at namespace scope needs static.

p02.why: The constant initializer of x reads u.f while u.i is the active member.

p03.why: The anonymous union has a member i, and the enclosing class S already has a member i.

p04.why: The assignment to u.a.tag makes a active but leaves u.a.a with no value, and constant evaluation reads that part.

p05.why: Item has a virtual destructor, which is non-trivial, so the destructor of Slot is deleted and the variable s uses it.

p06.why: S has a user-provided destructor, so the destructor of U is deleted and the variable u uses it.

p07.why: A bit-field must not be static.

p08.why: A bit-field must not be a typedef.

p09.why: A union must not have a member of reference type.

p10.why: An anonymous union at namespace scope needs static, also in an unnamed namespace.

p11.why: The braced initializer converts the non-constant int v to the declared type unsigned, which narrows.

p12.why: The constructor has mem_init entries for two variant members, i and f.

p13.why: The braced initializer for the first member c narrows the constant 1000 to char.

p14.why: S has a user-provided copy constructor, so the copy constructor of U is deleted and b(a) uses it.

p15.why: Item has a user-provided move constructor, so the move constructor of Slot is deleted and the initialization of b uses it.

p16.why: Item has a user-provided copy assignment, so the copy assignment of Slot is deleted and b = a uses it.

p17.why: A bit-field must have an integral or enumeration type, and float is neither.

p18.why: An anonymous union must not have member functions.

p19.why: Default initialization of s gives the union no active member, and constant evaluation reads s.count.

p20.why: Part has a user-provided destructor, so Item's destructor is non-trivial, the destructor of Slot is deleted, and s uses it.

p21.why: N has a non-trivial default constructor, so w.n.x = 4 does not make n active, and the assignment uses an object that does not exist during constant evaluation.

p22.why: A bit-field must have an integral or enumeration type, and int* is a pointer.

p23.why: Item has a user-provided copy constructor, so the copy constructor of Slot is deleted and b = a uses it.

p24.why: An anonymous union must not have nested types.

p25.why: The Holder constructor does not initialize slot, so slot has no active member, and constant evaluation reads h.slot.count.

p26.why: The compound assignment u.l += 1 reads l, which is not active, during constant evaluation.

p27.why: u.t = 5 calls a user-provided assignment operator on t while i is active, so it uses an object that does not exist yet.

p28.why: A bit-field must not have a negative width.

p29.why: Item has a virtual function, so its copy constructor is non-trivial, the copy constructor of Slot is deleted, and b = a uses it.

p30.why: M has a user-provided default constructor, so the default constructor of S, which has an anonymous union member with M, is deleted, and s uses it.

p31.why: A program must not take the address of a bit-field.

p32.why: An anonymous union must not have static data members.

p33.why: The members of an anonymous union must all be public, and i is private.

p34.why: Part has a user-provided copy constructor, so Item's copy is non-trivial, the copy constructor of Slot is deleted, and b = a uses it.

p35.why: The width w is a variable that is not usable in constant expressions, so the width is not a constant.

p36.why: Two variant members, i and f, have default member initializers.

p37.why: A bit-field must not have width 0 and a name.

p38.why: The assignment u.f = 2.0f makes f active, so the later read of u.i reads an inactive member during constant evaluation.

p39.why: The braced list gives two initializers to a union.

p40.why: Constant evaluation does not permit a read of tag through the inactive struct b, even though tag is in the common initial sequence.

p41.why: A program must not bind a non-const reference to a bit-field.

p42.why: A program must not apply sizeof to a bit-field.

p43.why: S has a user-provided default constructor and destructor, so those of U are deleted, and u uses both.

p44.why: The braced list has two designators for one union.

p45.why: Item has a virtual base, so its copy constructor is non-trivial, the copy constructor of Slot is deleted, and b = a uses it.

p46.why: Item has a user-provided destructor, so the destructor of Slot is deleted and s uses it.
